newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Firing squad yielding to injections in Guatemala.
newsitem.headline: Firing squad yielding to injections in Guatemala.

text.p: Guatemalan prison authorities on Monday unveiled a modern lethal injection chamber to replace the firing squad.

The $69,000 chamber was ordered after the initial rifle shots in a televised execution by firing squad last year failed to kill two condemned prisoners, who were finished off with close-range pistol shots to the head.

"People sentenced to death can come to this module and be executed according to the law," Deputy Interior Minister Salvador Gandara told reporters at the Pavon Rehabilitation Farm just outside the capital.
Guatemala is the only Central American nation with the death penalty. Most Guatemalans support it, but many felt the firing squad gave the country a bad image.
Local television stations incessantly replayed gruesome images of the execution of two men convicted of raping and killing a 4-year-old girl.
In reaction to the media coverage, Congress passed a law in October changing the death penalty method to lethal injection.

The 66-by-23-foot (20-by-7-metre) death chamber has an observation room for prison and justice system authorities, a room for the medical team that will administer the injection, and a cell for the prisoner.
A handful of convicted murderers and kidnappers has been condemned to die and is in the process of appealing sentences. The death penalty for kidnappers has been on the books since April 1996.
Hundreds of accused kidnappers are in jail awaiting trial, and officials anticipate the courts will be handling dozens of death penalty sentences and appeals in the coming months.
